The len(body) > 1_000_000 guard in get() can never fire because the read is already capped.
PARTIAL_DATA_BANNER.FIX: Fetch closed PRs with a page size that keeps each page well below the cap, stop paging once MAX_MERGES merged rows are collected, and detect oversize bodies honestly (read limit+1 bytes; over the limit raises a distinct 'too_large' reason) for every endpoint.

NODE.TITLE: Reproduce the three Command Center defects from the live snapshot and code
NODE.QUESTION: What exactly produces the 'Partial source data · error' banner, the doubled Omega-Prime main card and the 'unknown' Greptile text, and why do status buckets and task clicks not open their own views, on feat/command-center ad3942b?

RATIONALE.STEP: Read the live /api/snapshot from 127.0.0.1:7421 (read-only): sources.github.command_center.meta.errors is ['recent_merges:error'], sections.recent_merges is partial with reason 'error', and repositories plus ci_cd are clean.
Trace 'error' in collectors/github.py fail(): it is the label for ValueError/JSONDecodeError, so the recent-merges request returned a body that could not be parsed, not an HTTP or budget failure.

Measure the closed-PR page: GET /repos/swcstudiospace/Omega-Prime/pulls?state=closed&per_page=100 returns about 1.17 MB, but _request() reads at most 1,000,000 bytes, so the JSON is cut off and json.loads fails; the later len(body) > 1_000_000 guard can never fire.

Count branch rows: the backend ci_cd list already holds one kind='branch' row per target (Omega-Prime main and coding-fleet main), and frontend views/CiCd.tsx also synthesises a branch row from repositories[].latest_main_ci, so every default branch renders twice.

Trace the Greptile text: backend branch rows carry greptile_review null and the CiCard renders 'Score unknown · Review source unknown · reviewed SHA unknown · head match unknown'; PR rows whose score came from the body marker also show reviewed SHA and head match as unknown.

Map navigation: App.tsx keeps view and selection in useState only (no URL), Overview's SummaryCards (Active work, Waiting on Ove, PR gate, Finished) are static, non-clickable cards, and the sidebar WORK QUEUE only switches to the Tasks view with a shared detail pane, so no bucket or task has its own view or deep link.

Map the Herdr side: collectors/herdr.py runs 'herdr api snapshot' and lists panes (pane_id, workspace, agent_status, cwd, terminal_title, session_path); the box herdr CLI offers 'herdr pane read <PANE_ID> --source recent --lines N --format text' for read-only output; task records (types.ts Task) carry owner{kind,ref,label}, wiring and links but no Herdr pane field.

NODE.CONCLUSION: Confirmed root causes: (1) the 1 MB read cap truncates the ~1.17 MB Omega-Prime closed-PR page, so recent_merges fails as 'error'; (2) CiCd.tsx adds a synthetic default-branch row on top of the backend's branch row; (3) branch rows have no Greptile data and the card prints 'unknown'; (4) navigation is in-memory state with static summary cards, so buckets and tasks have no own view or URL; (5) a read-only pane read exists in the herdr CLI, but tasks are not yet mapped to panes.

NODE.TITLE: Choose the recent-merges fetch fix
NODE.QUESTION: How should recent merges be fetched so a large closed-PR page never truncates into a parse error?

RATIONALE.STEP: Option 1: lower per_page for the closed-PR listing (for example 30) so each page stays far under 1 MB; simple, but long PR bodies could still exceed the cap one day.
Option 2: read cap+1 bytes and raise a dedicated 'too_large' error when the body is over the cap, so an oversized page is reported honestly instead of as 'error'.
Option 3: stop paging once MAX_MERGES merged rows are collected, since only the newest 100 merges are shown, which cuts calls and bytes.

Pick 1 + 2 + 3 together: a smaller page size for the closed listing, explicit oversize detection in _request() for every endpoint, and early stop at MAX_MERGES; keep the 2.5 s per-request timeout and the 12 s collector deadline.

Regression test: a fake transport returning a 1.2 MB closed page must not produce 'recent_merges:error'; a fake that is truly over the cap must yield reason 'too_large' and keep the previous merges (stale) rather than wiping them.

NODE.CONCLUSION: Use a smaller closed-PR page size, detect oversize bodies explicitly (read limit+1 → 'too_large'), and stop paging once MAX_MERGES merges are gathered. Tests cover the 1.2 MB case and the oversize-fallback case.

NODE.TITLE: Design de-duplicated CI/CD cards and branch-row Greptile state
NODE.QUESTION: How do we show each default branch once and give branch rows a Greptile value that is not 'unknown'?

RATIONALE.STEP: De-duplicate in CiCd.tsx by key repo + branch + head_sha: take backend ci_cd rows first, then add a synthetic latest_main_ci row only for repos with no matching branch row; also de-duplicate React keys.

Backend branch rows: call GET /repos/{repo}/commits/{sha}/pulls (bounded, inside the existing budget and deadline) and, when exactly one merged PR targets the default branch, reuse _greptile() on it with source 'merged_pr' and that PR's number.
When no PR links to the head commit, set greptile_review to {score: null, source: 'not_applicable'} so the UI can say 'No PR review · direct commit' instead of four 'unknown' fields.
In the CiCard, render branch rows as 'Greptile N/5 · from #PR' or 'No PR review for this commit', and for PR rows with a body-marker score show 'reviewed SHA not reported' rather than 'unknown'.
Keep every new field redacted through redact_value, accept only https://github.com URLs via _safe_url, and treat a failed lookup as 'unavailable' without marking the whole ci_cd section partial.

NODE.CONCLUSION: Frontend de-duplicates by repo+branch+SHA with backend rows winning. Backend enriches branch rows from the commit's merged PR via commits/{sha}/pulls, else marks them not_applicable. The UI shows clear wording for each state; a failed lookup never flips the section to partial.

NODE.TITLE: Design the read-only live Herdr terminal panel in the task view
NODE.QUESTION: How can the task detail view show a live, read-only view of the task's Herdr session safely from the local server?

RATIONALE.STEP: Mapping: add an optional herdr_pane field (pane id, optionally workspace) to the task record, validated in status_file against a strict pane-id pattern; when it is missing, fall back to owner.kind/owner.ref only if the owner names a Herdr pane; otherwise the panel shows 'No session attached'.

Capture: the server runs 'herdr pane read <pane> --source recent --lines 200 --format text' as an argv list (never a shell), with a short timeout, about once a second, only while a viewer is connected; the browser never sends a pane id, only the task id.

Endpoint: GET /api/tasks/{task_id}/terminal (SSE) on the existing 127.0.0.1-only server, behind the same Host check, GET-only guard and CSP; it emits a frame only when the redacted text changes, plus heartbeats, and caps concurrent terminal streams.

Sanitise: strip ANSI and control sequences on the server (render plain text, no HTML), cap each frame to the last 200 lines and 64 KB, and pass it through redact_value plus token patterns (bearer, ghp_/github_pat_, sk-, JWT-like strings, KEY=value lines) before it leaves the process.

Read-only by construction: no input endpoint, no WebSocket, no send-text/send-keys call anywhere, a terminal element that is a <pre> with no input focus, and a test that asserts the server never invokes any herdr input subcommand.

UI: a TerminalPanel in the task detail page with a live dot, last-updated time, pause/resume of auto-scroll, copy, and clear states for no session attached, pane closed, Herdr unavailable and stream reconnecting.
Tests: Python tests with a fake runner for mapping, argv shape, ANSI stripping, caps, redaction and the no-input guarantee; Vitest for the panel states and SSE reconnect.

NODE.CONCLUSION: Tasks map to panes through a validated herdr_pane field. The 127.0.0.1 server reads the pane with 'herdr pane read' (argv, timeout, only while watched), strips ANSI, caps to 200 lines/64 KB, redacts secrets and streams changes over SSE at /api/tasks/{id}/terminal. There is no input path anywhere, and the panel shows clear states when no session is attached.

NODE.TITLE: Critique risks: budget, security, terminal exposure, cache merging and the parallel 7421 move
NODE.QUESTION: What could make this polish regress the dashboard or collide with the live server move?

RATIONALE.STEP: API budget: the extra commits/{sha}/pulls call adds one request per target per refresh plus up to two Greptile pages; it fits the 1000-call budget and 90 s cache, but must respect the 12 s deadline.

Security: keep loopback bind, Host check, CSP, GET-only, no redirects and token redaction; new fields go through redact_value and _safe_url, and nothing new reaches the browser that contains the token.
Stale cache merging: the partial-section merge logic re-uses old rows for failed repos; the de-duplication must also hold when old and new branch rows mix after a partial refresh.

Parallel work: another worker is moving the Command Center onto 127.0.0.1:7421 from /workspace/omes-bot-wt/cc with Ove's real home, so this build must never touch that worktree, that port or ~/.omega-prime/dashboard; test on 7441 with a throwaway HOME.

Route risk: the omp-sandbox run (Sol plans, Luna builds on the ChatGPT plan) previously failed on GSD helpers and npm egress; reuse omp-sandbox fixes ca1dac4, 43b8797 and 002bea1, and fall back to local omp only if the sandbox fails again.

Terminal exposure: pane output can hold secrets, so redaction runs server-side before SSE, frames are capped, streams are loopback-only behind the Host check, and the endpoint resolves panes only from task records, so a browser cannot read an arbitrary pane; subprocess load is bounded by polling only while watched and capping streams.

Routing risk: hash routes avoid a server SPA fallback and keep the CSP unchanged; deep links to unknown tasks or buckets must render a not-found state, and existing tests for the static views must keep passing.

NODE.CONCLUSION: Risks are bounded: one extra GitHub call per target, unchanged security posture, a terminal path that is read-only, loopback-only, redacted and capped, routes that need no server change, de-duplication robust to stale-cache mixing, strict isolation from the 7421 move, and the known sandbox fixes.
